angle: You can’t outbid churn; impact, autonomy, and shipping to production keep builders.
sourceTitle: What Gets Your Best Employees to Stay
linkedinPost:
You can’t outbid churn.

MIT Sloan Management Review notes that even eye-popping comp couldn’t stop high-profile defections at top AI shops. If they can’t buy retention, neither can you. Money opens the door; impact and autonomy keep people in the room.

What actually works in AI orgs I’ve seen stick:

- Ship to production fast. Builders stay where their work touches customers, not slide decks.
- Protect “maker time.” Cap meeting load; measure and defend uninterrupted build hours.
- Clear pathways to technical leadership without people management. Don’t force ICs into manager chairs.
- Internal mobility, not hero projects. Move talent to the next valuable problem before recruiters do.
- Transparent governance. Nothing kills morale like unclear risk rules that change at the 11th hour.

My take: Retention is an operating system, not a perk. Track time-to-impact, percent of work in prod, and voluntary internal moves like core KPIs. And make managers accountable for them.

If one lever had to move this quarter: what would you change to help your AI builders ship more and meet less? #AIAdoption #EnterpriseAI #AIStrategy
